newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BYU BEATS KANSAS STATE IN COTTON BOWL.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BYU BEATS KANSAS STATE IN COTTON BOWL.

text.p: Ko Kealaluhi caught a 28-yard touchdown pass with 3:38 left as fifth-ranked Brigham Young overcame a 10-point deficit to defeat 14th-ranked Kansas State, 19-15, in the Cotton Bowl on Wednesday.

Quarterback Brian Kavanagh drove Kansas State to the Brigham Young 14 but was intercepted by Omarr Morgan at the 3-yard line with just under a minute remaining to preserve the victory, a record 14th of the season for BYU.

Despite being sacked seven times by the vaunted Kansas State defence, quarterback Steve Sarkisian completed 21-of-36 passes for 291 yards and two touchdowns for the Cougars (14-1), who were bypassed by the bowl alliance and settled for the trip to Dallas in its first New Year's Day appearance. The snub cost BYU over $6 million in bowl revenue.
Kavanagh completed 14-of-28 for 233 yards and two touchdowns, but was intercepted twice and sacked four times.

Kansas State (9-3) took a 15-5 lead with 9:10 remaining in the third quarter when Kevin Lockett caught a pass from Kavanagh, broke a tackle and ran down the right sideline to complete a 72-yard scoring play. Lockett caught seven passes for 135 yards.
The Cougars cut the lead to 15-12 with 10:55 left in the game when James Dye caught a 32-yard pass from Sarkisian.

Brigham Young jumped to a 5-0 first-quarter lead. Kavanagh took a snap from the shotgun, rolled right and was tackled in the end zone by linebacker Shay Muirbrook for a safety. Ethan Pochman added a 39-yard field goal less than two minutes later.

Andre Anderson's 41-yard "Hail Mary" touchdown catch as time expired in the first half gave Kansas State its first lead. Kavanagh lofted the pass into the end zone, where it was tipped by a BYU defender into the arms of a falling Anderson.

The teams headed to the locker rooms, but an offsides penalty called after the extra point brought them back onto the field. The Wildcats decided to go for two points and Mike Lawrence ran it in off right end to give Kansas State a three-point lead at the half.
